title: CapturePack annotations.json
description: Schema for annotations.json, the OPTIONAL editable annotation layer of a CapturePack (format 0.1.0). Format 0.1.0 defines exactly one annotation type: the box. A box composes its roles through properties — numbered:true makes it a numbered marker, blur:true marks a sensitive region, text carries its description; any combination is valid on one box. Annotations are stored as data, editable forever, and are NEVER burned into the original media: snapshot.png and the replay always keep original pixels, and blur renders only into derived views such as replay_annotated (SPEC.md §9). Display numbers are computed from the numbered boxes (SPEC.md §8.5), never stored. All geometry is in snapshot pixel coordinates: origin at the top-left pixel of snapshot.png, x right, y down, units are snapshot pixels; coordinates may be non-integers. Unknown additional properties are deliberately allowed for forward compatibility, but this schema only accepts the "box" type — a pack using a newer type fails validation here while remaining readable under the defensive-reading rules (SPEC.md §13). See SPEC.md §8 for the normative definition; where schema and prose disagree, the prose wins.

reference_width.description: Width in pixels of the annotation coordinate space. MUST equal the pixel width of snapshot.png. If a reader finds the actual snapshot dimensions differ (e.g. the image was rescaled by an intermediate tool), it SHOULD scale all geometry by actual/reference per axis rather than discard the annotations.

reference_height.description: Height in pixels of the annotation coordinate space. MUST equal the pixel height of snapshot.png.

annotations.description: List of annotation boxes. May be empty. Array order carries no meaning — reading order is defined by the display-number rule (SPEC.md §8.5) and lifetimes, not by array position.

box.description: One annotation box — the only annotation type in format 0.1.0. Readers MUST skip annotations of unknown type and SHOULD preserve them when rewriting a pack.

annotation_id.description: Permanent identity of the annotation: the literal prefix "ann_" plus 6 lowercase hex digits, e.g. "ann_8f21c4". MUST be unique within this file. Referenced by timeline events (core.annotation.added), documents, and MCP responses. The id never changes; display numbers do (SPEC.md §8.5).

type.description: The annotation type. MUST be "box" in format 0.1.0.

bounds.description: The box rectangle in snapshot pixel coordinates. width and height MUST be > 0.

x.description: Top-left corner X, in snapshot pixels.

y.description: Top-left corner Y, in snapshot pixels.

text.description: The box's description — what the user typed. MAY be empty; absent means "".

start_ms.description: Start of the box's lifetime — the closed interval [start_ms, end_ms] of the replay clock during which the box applies, in milliseconds (SPEC.md §8.4). MUST be <= end_ms, and MUST appear together with end_ms (both or neither; enforced below via dependentRequired). Absent lifetime = the box applies to the whole capture. Only meaningful when the pack has a replay; both bounds SHOULD lie within [0, replay_duration_ms]. When a single representative instant is needed, it is the lifetime midpoint (start_ms + end_ms) / 2 — there is no separately stored anchor.

end_ms.description: End of the box's lifetime, in milliseconds on the replay clock (SPEC.md §8.4). MUST be >= start_ms, and MUST appear together with start_ms (both or neither). Viewers and the annotated-replay renderer draw a box only while the current position lies inside its lifetime; boxes without a lifetime always draw. Blur applies exactly during the lifetime (SPEC.md §9).

numbered.description: Whether the box takes part in display numbering (SPEC.md §8.5). Default false. The number itself is NEVER stored — it is computed: numbered boxes sorted by start_ms ascending (absent lifetime = 0), then z ascending (absent z = array position), then annotation_id ascending, numbered contiguously from 1. Every consumer (editor, replay_annotated, report.md, README.md, skills/, MCP) MUST use exactly this rule.

blur.description: Whether the box's interior is sensitive and MUST be blurred in rendered views (SPEC.md §9). Default false. Blur is non-destructive: snapshot.png and the replay keep the original, unredacted pixels; blur renders only into derived views (replay_annotated, editor previews), during the box's lifetime, moving with the box, and before any other annotation layer is drawn.

tracking.description: Object-tracking state. In format 0.1.0 the only defined field is 'enabled', and it MUST be false — frame-by-frame tracking data (bounds following a moving object) is reserved for a future version. Absent means { "enabled": false }. Readers MUST ignore tracking content they do not understand and treat the box as untracked.

enabled.description: Whether the box tracks a moving object. MUST be false in format 0.1.0.

target.description: RESERVED for semantic object metadata: what real UI object the box points at (DOM selector/role/text, Windows UI Automation AutomationId/ControlType, engine object ids, ...). This is where the earlier draft's 'element'/Tracked Element concept lives — a box with a target is a semantic annotation; there is no separate element type. Format 0.1.0 does not define its contents; readers MUST ignore what they do not understand and MUST still render the box from bounds.

style.description: OPTIONAL display styling. In 0.1.0 the only defined field is 'color', used for the border, number badge, and text. Viewers pick their own default when absent.

color.description: Display color as CSS-style hex: "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA".

created_at.description: OPTIONAL creation instant of the annotation, ISO 8601 with timezone.

z.description: OPTIONAL stacking order for rendering; higher draws on top. Also the second tiebreaker in display numbering (SPEC.md §8.5). Default: the annotation's array position (later entries render on top).
